name: Cybercrime Directive
summary: The Commission's 2017 report found that the Directive had led to comparable criminal offences for cyberattacks across Member States, but that definitions, penalties and statistics were not fully implemented; it saw no need to amend the Directive. The Directive's own statistics requirement is the weakest point, so its effect on cybercrime cannot be measured.

indicators.objective: No monitoring indicators set in the proposal; assessed through the Commission's reports listed below

indicators.evidence: 2017 report: statistics and reporting channels among the provisions least implemented.

literature.citation: European Commission (2017), Report assessing the extent to which the Member States have taken the necessary measures to comply with Directive 2013/40/EU on attacks against information systems, COM(2017) 474
literature.title: Report assessing the extent to which the Member States have taken the necessary measures to comply with Directive 2013/40/EU on attacks against information systems
literature.headline: Substantive progress in criminalising cyberattacks on a comparable level; gaps on definitions, penalties, reporting channels and statistics; no need to amend
literature.summary_plain: The Commission found that countries had made cyberattacks crimes on similar terms, but had not fully applied the rules on penalties and statistics.
